claim: Alan's framework for ordering his dependencies is settled — criticality times likelihood of degrading times cost of leaving, each scored one to four — and the sorted list it exists to produce has never been made. No page holds the household's dependencies with their three scores and their product. What the book carries instead is a scatter of per-domain firsts: solar the highest-leverage purchase, the garden the highest-leverage food move, the umbrella the highest-leverage insurance move, each ranked inside its own domain and none against the others. So what to remediate first is decided domain by domain rather than by the instrument built to decide it.

evidence:
Read across `alan/book/pages/all-about-alan/topic/pages/` and `.../question/pages/`.

The instrument. `which-dependency-i-deal-with-first`: "I order the list by how critical the thing is, times how likely they are to degrade, times what leaving would cost me… Each factor gets one to four, so the product runs one to sixty-four." Each factor has its own page — `how-critical-a-dependency-is`, `how-likely-they-are-to-get-worse`, `what-leaving-a-dependency-costs-me`.

The list. No page carries it. No dependency anywhere in the book is given its three scores or its product, and no question asks for the list to be made.

What is there instead is a first inside each domain. `the-solar-on-the-roof` calls solar the highest-leverage thing he can buy; `the-garden-we-do-not-eat-from` calls the garden "the highest-leverage move I have toward feeding ourselves"; `the-umbrella-i-have-not-bought` calls the umbrella "the highest-leverage move open to me here". None of the three is scored, and none is set against the other two.

The book knows the instrument is not finished. `a-dependency-that-only-exists-for-another-one`: "My ranking still treats each one separately, which is a gap in the ranking." `how-much-of-me-is-on-one-provider`: concentration is "what orders my queue rather than what sets the letter", and the queue it would order is nowhere. `where-a-concentration-fits-in-my-ranking` and `whether-a-switching-cascade-is-its-own-cost` are the open questions on it.

Not measured: that priorities are decided domain by domain is my reading of the per-domain firsts, not something Alan has said. I did not score any dependency myself.
